result: STAR UCT USES TAP-TO-PLACE; TRADINGVIEW USES A DRAGGABLE CURSOR WITH A LIVE READOUT
url: self-measured live; storage delta confirmed before and after
notes: STAR THE CORE EVIDENCE FOR PRIMITIVE P1, MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES. TradingView's placement grammar is: a cursor object you DRAG, with every dependent value recomputing live under the finger (TV-IOS-REPLAY-0003 drags a replay cursor and the whole indicator legend stack follows). UCT's is: your fingertip IS the commit. On a 390px chart where one vertical pixel is roughly 0.6 of a dollar on this symbol, tap-to-place means the level you get is the level your finger landed on, and the only correction is to delete and retry. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ARCHITECTURAL DIFFERENCE FOUND, and it is not a feature gap - it is a different answer to the same physics.
